what: One public repository for the code
why: Two copies (private and public) drifted in 21 source files and were synced by hand-porting patches, so fixes came back and features went missing
evidence: Reconciling showed public was a superset: private-only lines were older code or real names already replaced with invented ones; 3 demo tweaks ported
result: Code, docs, CI and this log live here; maxwell-private keeps user research, launch material and real-data fixtures only (decisions before 2026-11-15 are in its log)

what: Engineering standard with a ratchet check
why: 22 releases and many regressions on 2026-11-15; knowledge split across account memories
evidence: scripts/check-standard.py: planted violations fail, clean tree passes; it caught another merge growing main.swift by 73 lines within 30 minutes
result: docs/engineering-standard.md and docs/cleanup-plan.md; the check runs in ./build.sh test, so in CI on every PR and in every release

what: CI on every pull request
why: Tests only ran inside the release, after merging
evidence: macOS runner, same image as the release; free for a public repository
result: .github/workflows/ci.yml: standard check, tests and a full Maxwell Dev build

what: Groups pass a soak test (0.1.40): Stop while Claude Code still reports work stays Working until it confirms; a background turn's verdict is waited for and used only when written for this turn; notifications fire once a state held 1.5 s and never repeat the same question; watchers aren't work; a clean Stop clears an earlier limit; a finished session with a server running is Your turn; '! N unverified' when Claude Code's files can't be read; Maxwell watch
why: The groups must be trusted; one snapshot check was not enough, and the standard asks for events, not timers
evidence: Scripted background sessions (plain, background shell, async subagent, permission prompt approved via attach, AskUserQuestion, Esc, question without status line, blocked with a shell, dev server) compared against Claude Code's own files every 0.25 s: before, 3 false done notifications and the permission text overwritten; after two rounds, every change matched within 0.3 s with one notification each. An independent review's 8 findings fixed with tests
result: pass

what: Panel tabs always on the stripe (0.1.42): every panel of a side keeps its tab, lit while open; clicking a lit tab hides it
why: A tab vanished as soon as its panel opened, so the edge kept changing under the pointer
evidence: Maxwell Dev snapshots: Viewer and Plugins tabs stay; clicking Viewer opens and lights it, clicking Plugins hides it and its tab stays dim
result: pass

what: Quiet runs keep their windows off every screen
why: Test runs and session-started Maxwell Dev kept their window behind the user's, still on screen, and a run reopened by `open` lost --quit-after and came to the front over Robin's work
evidence: Parked at x past every screen's right edge: --snap captures at 2x, the front app never changes during a run, Settings and sign-in windows go the same way; a test run started with --quit-after 52 was found front-most 77 min later after being reopened
result: MXWindow.present parks quiet windows; quiet runs post no notifications; --retina moves the window only if its scale is wrong; .claude/settings.json refuses `open … Maxwell` from a session

what: Side panels are tabs (0.1.45): a side area shows one list or document at a time; opening one hides the others there, widgets still stack
why: Viewer and plugins stacked in one column left each too short to use; asked for tab behaviour
evidence: Maxwell Dev snapshots: clicking Viewer showed only the viewer with Plugins dim; clicking Plugins showed only plugins with Viewer dim
result: pass

what: Quiet runs end and never hold the front
why: A quiet run reopened by `open` cancelled its --quit-after and sat in front for over an hour; a session-started run without --quit-after never ended; --fullscreen took a Space; --select matched only the generated name and logged success anyway
evidence: Reopen during a run: ignored and quit on time; macOS still made it front for an instant, AppKit reported no activation, a workspace observer handed the front back (polled every 0.1 s: never Maxwell Dev); --select by shown title opens it, unknown names log 'no such session'
result: Quiet runs ignore reopen, quit after 10 min by default, skip --fullscreen and give the front back; --select matches the shown title

what: ⌘N starts with the project (0.1.41): inside a project it is picked; from All projects nothing is picked until you pick; search covers session folders plus git repos in the usual code folders; home and loose folders warn
why: A user's sessions landed in another project's folder and in ~ (3 of 6 in one recording) because ⌘N reused the last-viewed session's folder and offered only 5 recent folders; the workaround was a terminal and cd
evidence: Comparable apps (Zed, Codex, Conductor, Claude desktop) start new work from a project list, not a folder dialog; Maxwell Dev snapshots of All projects, a scoped project, typing, and ⌘T on All projects
result: pass; ⌘T on All projects with nothing open now asks too

what: A claude in a Maxwell terminal takes over that terminal's row (0.1.43)
why: Running claude in a Maxwell terminal showed two rows, the session's read-only and offering Bring into Maxwell
evidence: Terminals carry MAXWELL_TERMINAL; matched from the hook's pid via sysctl KERN_PROCARGS2 (system binaries hide their environment, claude does not); Zed's Terminal Threads do the same; Maxwell Dev run: one row with the live terminal, terminal row back when claude exits
result: pass; no hook or reducer change, so sessions already running match too

what: `open -a Maxwell .` starts a session there (0.1.44)
why: Developers start in a terminal already in the right folder; Claude desktop (`claude --desktop`) and Codex (`codex app`) offer the same
evidence: Folder document type with handler rank None; quiet `open -g -a … <repo>` run shows the panel with the repo picked
result: pass; no command to install on PATH

what: Pins and marks (0.1.46): right-click Pin to Top (listed first, never in Close all) and Mark As Your turn, Safe to close or Idle, holding until the next turn; Close all covers only the open project; the hook hands the status-line rule to sessions that started before it on their next prompt
why: A session from another project was offered in Close all, a wrongly safe session could only be kept with a button that lapsed on any activity, and every session of one project missing the status line had started before the rule existed (checked in events.jsonl: all started before 15:31, the first status line)
evidence: Reducer tests for marks, pins and the old not-safe line; hook run on sample payloads; Maxwell Dev snapshots of Pinned, a marked row and its banner, and Close all scoped to one project without its pinned session
result: pass

what: Let go of terminals off screen for 10 minutes
why: Claude Code stops an idle background session only when nothing is attached, and Maxwell kept every terminal it opened attached until it quit, so idle sessions never freed their memory
evidence: On one Mac: 31 background sessions held 11.4 GB while 9 worked; Maxwell held 15 `claude attach` processes; the service's log showed a session it stopped after 8 hours idle that Maxwell attached again
result: TerminalRelease: off screen 10 minutes, let go; opening the session attaches again

what: A session Claude Code stops while it waits on you is parked, not ended
why: A stopped session leaves `claude agents --json`, which Maxwell read as ended, so a session waiting on you vanished from Your turn after an hour without an attached terminal
evidence: `claude agents --json --all` lists such a session as done; `claude stop` on it exits 0; `claude attach` resumes it (2.1.325)
result: It keeps its group; opening it shows the last reply and Resume instead of starting it again; parked long ago it folds into Idle

what: Grey text passes WCAG AA in every theme
why: fg3 (secondary labels, ages, sources) measured 3.3 to 4.4 against the panel, under 4.5 for small text
evidence: Contrast against background and panel, computed per theme
result: graphite #80858d, paper #6c6e75, silver #878d95, silver-light #61666f

what: A Safe to close status line skips the Haiku read
why: Robin: sessions that said Safe to close still sat in Your turn. The read vetoed them over caveats and notes, and was not stable: three reruns of one reply gave pending, pending, finished; the log has one reply judged finished then unsure
evidence: Real log: 43 reads, 24 not finished; 8 of those replies ended in Safe to close (v0.1.42 shipped, replied ok, ...). Tests: a safe status line with a pending or unsure read is safe; with no read it is safe and no read is asked
result: Verdict.checks adds no judge check when the status line check passes; judgeCandidates skips those; judge = off still means never safe; replies without a status line keep the read

what: Cloud sessions read from the Sessions API with Claude Code's own login
why: claude agents doesn't list cloud sessions and attaching a terminal to one is off for these accounts, so Maxwell had no way to see their state
evidence: GET /v1/sessions with the account's Keychain token returns status, Claude's turn summary and branch (2.1.325); archive, claude --cloud under script, claude -p --cloud and --teleport checked live
result: Sources/ClaudeCode/CloudSessions.swift reads, Sources/Model/Cloud.swift maps to groups; never Safe to close; the page shows in the pane

what: Send to Cloud goes through a brief, not a move
why: claude --cloud --resume refuses local session ids here, and /teleport's move needs Remote Control and restarts background sessions
evidence: A haiku test session asked with the wrap-up prompt replied with goal, done, left, check and branch
result: The session commits, pushes and writes the brief; Maxwell refuses unpushed work, waits out permission prompts and stops the local session only once the cloud one runs

what: Folder fills a narrow viewer with no file open
why: In a viewer under 620pt the folder slid in as a 280pt drawer over a dimmed page, and with no file open the rest was an empty dark strip
evidence: Reported screenshot showed the 280pt drawer beside a dimmed empty strip; in the demo world at 1000x700 the folder now spans the viewer; with a file open the drawer stays 280pt over the page
result: Sources/UI/Chrome.swift sizes the drawer to the viewer and drops the scrim when no item is shown; --click takes several clicks so the harness can open the viewer and then the folder

what: Terminals can be renamed
why: A user could not tell two terminals apart: both were named after their folder, and nothing let you change it
evidence: Right-click a terminal row in Maxwell Dev, Rename…, the row and the pane header show the new name
result: The name lives in memory until the terminal closes, like the terminal itself; empty goes back to the folder name. Session and terminal rename share one prompt

what: Window corners clipped to the window's radius
why: The main window is see-through and its content was never clipped to the rounded corners, so the rim macOS draws stair-stepped around a chamfered corner
evidence: Captured with frame and shadow on macOS 26: before, a stepped chamfer next to a plain window's round corner; after, the same round 20pt corner top and bottom. Clipping only the root view or only the content view left a chamfer: the glass and the tint both need it
result: MXWindow.clipCorners clips the glass and root view: 20pt on macOS 26, 10pt before, square in full screen. --snap leaves out the rim, so docs/harness.md says how to check corners

what: Terminals come back after a restart
why: A terminal you named or kept open in a folder vanished when Maxwell quit, while sessions came back; Warp and Terminal both restore theirs
evidence: Maxwell Dev: two terminals opened, quit, relaunched: both reopened in order without taking the selection; a saved name came back; a saved folder that no longer exists reopened in the nearest folder still there
result: Saved in UserDefaults (folder, name, order) on every change, not at quit, so a crash keeps them. Shells start fresh: no scrollback yet (Warp keeps the last blocks; ours would need Ghostty to hand over its buffer). Double-click renames, as in Warp and Finder. Demo and screenshot scripts clear the list so takes start the same

what: Terminals act like sessions: tabs, search, rename, undo
why: A terminal had no tab, search could not find it, rename was right-click only, and closing one (× or a running dev server) was final with no question
evidence: Maxwell Dev: a terminal gets a ❯ tab; ⌘P lists it as terminal · folder; closing an idle one shows Closed … Undo and Undo brings it back in place; closing with sleep running logs a command is running, asking
result: confirm-close-surface is now true: Maxwell's close callback ignores it, it only makes ghostty_surface_needs_confirm_quit answer (it said false while a command ran). Closing a terminal's tab keeps it running, as for sessions; × , Close Terminal and ⌘⇧⌫ end it. Terminal code moved to MainWindow+Terminals.swift

what: A plain click on a file path in a session opens it in the viewer
why: Paths in a session's replies looked plain and only ⌘-click opened them, which nobody found; Claude Code takes plain clicks for itself
evidence: Maxwell Dev in the demo world: hovering docs/dark-mode-plan.md showed the hand and underline, a click opened it in its own viewer tab; a web link and a missing file were not claimed and their clicks went through. FileLink tests cover trailing punctuation, :line:col, ~, file:// URLs, folders and the second folder tried
result: Only files that exist are claimed, so a click on anything else still reaches Claude Code. Link lookup tries ⌘⇧ then ⌘: Ghostty wants shift added only while mouse reporting is on, and the demo's stand-in claude doesn't turn it on. Ghostty's underline keeps a trailing full stop; opening strips it

what: Artifact links open on the first click
why: A click on an artifact link with Maxwell in the background only brought the window forward; the next click arrived as a double click, which Maxwell passed to Claude Code, and Claude Code opened the link in the system browser
evidence: Maxwell Dev, a test world with mouse reporting on and an OSC 8 link, and a real Claude Code session: --plain-click reported 'background click lost, double click passed on' before the fix and 'background click opens, double click opens' after it
result: TerminalView accepts the first mouse only on a claimed link (any other first click only brings the window forward, as in Ghostty) and claims every click on the link, whatever its click count

what: Terminals bring back what they showed
why: A terminal came back after a restart empty, so its build log or server output was gone; Terminal and Warp bring theirs back
evidence: Maxwell Dev: coloured output, quit, three restarts with nothing typed: one restored divider, no stacked Last login lines, colour kept; Undo after closing brings the output back; closing an idle restored terminal does not ask, closing one running sleep asks and names sleep
result: Ghostty writes screen and scrollback as VT (write_screen_file:copy,vt); the path comes back through the clipboard callback, caught for that one call so the clipboard is untouched. Kept: last 5000 lines, 0600 files under ~/.local/state/maxwell/terminals/<app id>, written at quit and on close (for Undo). A new shell prints it under a dim divider; a restore nobody typed after is dropped so dividers do not stack. Running-command check now uses the terminal foreground process (as Terminal does): Ghostty prompt marks are missing in a shell started behind the replay, so confirm-close-surface goes back to false

what: Crash and hang reports go to Sentry
why: Crashes in the released app were invisible unless someone wrote in
evidence: Maxwell Dev with reporting forced on: --crash-test and --hang-test reached Sentry project maxwell (HTTP 200); the same events captured on disk held no path, user name, breadcrumb, locale or device name; a release dSYM uploaded and processed
result: Sentry 9.34.0 static xcframework, pinned by checksum; on by default in the released app only, crash-reports = off turns it off; no swizzling, breadcrumbs, tracing or PII; CrashScrub removes paths, quotes, emails and the user name; release.sh uploads the dSYM with SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN. Hang threshold 3 s

what: Link lookup asks Ghostty whether the mouse is captured
why: The 0.1.56 lookup tried ⌘⇧ and then ⌘ alone on every cell without a link; with Claude Code's mouse reporting on (confirmed with Claude Code 2.1.325), the ⌘-only probe reached Claude Code as pointer moves
evidence: Maxwell Dev with a real Haiku session: the hover reports mouse reporting on and finds the path with ⌘⇧ only; a click opens notes/release-check.md and the viewer's text reads it
result: The hovered terminal is watched after each Ghostty tick while the pointer is over it, so output or scrolling that moves the text drops or moves the underline instead of leaving it under other text
